title.value: Doubly Right Object Recognition: A Why Prompt for Visual Rationales
title.justification: The paper introduces a 'doubly right' benchmark for object recognition that requires models to provide not only the correct categorical predictions but also the correct rationales for these predictions.
title.quote: We propose a 'doubly right' object recognition benchmark, where the metric requires the model to simultaneously produce both the right labels as well as the right rationales.

extractions.description: This paper explores the capability of computer vision models to not only provide accurate categorical labels for objects in images but also to give correct rationales for their predictions. It introduces a benchmark for 'doubly right' object recognition and proposes a 'why prompt' approach to improve the ability of models to generate correct rationales by adapting language model insights into visual models. This approach aims to enhance explainability and user trust in AI systems.

primary_category.justification: The paper primarily focuses on improving explainability and rationale generation in computer vision models, which does not directly align with any of the existing eco-responsible categories provided such as climate change mitigation or adaptation.
primary_category.quote: Learning models that can explain their own decision is important for building trustworthy systems, especially in applications that require human-machine interactions.

secondary_categories.justification: There are no direct applications or discussions in the paper related to eco-responsible issues such as climate change or pollution.
secondary_categories.quote: Most models today are not evaluated on whether they get the prediction right for the right reasons.

primary_sub_category.justification: The research does not fit within the sub-categories designed for eco-responsible impacts, as it targets the advancement of AI explainability.
primary_sub_category.quote: We introduce a benchmark for doubly right object recognition, where computer vision models must predict both correct categorical labels as well as correct rationales.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The paper does not contribute to specific eco-friendly technological advancements but focuses on the cognitive and interpretative capabilities of AI.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Our benchmark is large, and covers many categories and datasets.

new_primary_category.justification: This research emphasizes the importance of making AI decisions interpretable and justifying the reasoning behind predictions. This area is becoming crucial for building trustworthy AI systems.
new_primary_category.quote: Learning models that can explain their own decision is important for building trustworthy systems, especially in applications that require human-machine interactions.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The paper focuses on generating accurate rationales for AI predictions, representing a significant sub-category in AI explainability.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: We propose a framework to explicitly transfer the chain-of-thought reasoning from NLP models into vision models.
